clue.text: Gaining unfair advantage getting ahead of others

definitions.meaning: pushing in ahead of one's turn is a way of taking an unfair advantage
literally moving in front of people waiting in a line

explanation.surface: Someone cheats their way to the front of the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both cheating one's way forward and literally stepping in front of people waiting in a line.

clue.text: Very soon a little while ago!

definitions.meaning: as in 'she left ...', meaning moments back

explanation.surface: A paradox: the same moment is both imminent and recent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used both for the immediate future (in South Africa and dialect) and the immediate past.

clue.text: Socialiser's drink

definitions.meaning: a socialiser is someone who mingles at parties; the 's stands for 'is'
a soft drink such as tonic added to spirits

explanation.surface: The party-goer's beverage of choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A good mingler at a party is called this, and so is the tonic or soda poured into spirits.

clue.text: No alternative reassertion about anger

indicators.note: no tells us the letters for 'alternative' are taken away from the fodder
about signals that the remaining letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: the word reassertion is taken as written, as the letter pool
or is the word introducing an alternative

explanation.surface: Restating one's case leaves no other option and stokes fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No alternative' removes OR from REASSERTION, leaving REASSETIN, which 'about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irate is being angry, so the noun for that state is anger.

clue.text: Man about to remove list in a plucky way north of the border

definitions.text: in a plucky way north of the border

indicators.note: about places the man's letters around the other piece

parts.note: guy is an everyday word for a man

indicators.note: re-move, to move again, signals the letters of list are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fellow is about to strike something off a list, bravely, in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' read as re-move rearranges LIST into TSIL, which GUY goes 'about'. The Scottish tag adds colour; the core sense is bravely.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with guts means acting bravely and with nerve.

clue.text: She isn't the possessive type

parts.note: seems to describe a woman free of jealousy, but means a poor person who owns nothing

explanation.surface: A woman who is not jealous or clingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor person, one lacking possessions, is contrasted with the wealthy 'haves'.

clue.text: Sort of status extremely tough it was said

parts.note: status quo is a kind of status, so the word quo fills the gap

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of the word tough

explanation.surface: Some kind of standing proves very hard, reportedly.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic past form meaning 'said', as in 'quoth the raven'.

clue.text: Inspecting digging after chopper had been raised

indicators.note: after puts the word for digging later than the chopper piece
in a down clue, raising a word writes it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: an axe is a tool for chopping
mining is digging for ore

explanation.surface: Someone checks the digging site after an axe has been lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had been raised' turns AXE into EXA, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspecting something closely is studying or scrutinising it.

clue.text: Prophet found canal after second half of freeze

indicators.note: after places the canal after the piece from freeze
the second half of a six-letter word is its last three letters

parts.note: the Kiel Canal links the North Sea and the Baltic in Germany

explanation.surface: A holy man turns up a waterway once the cold snap is half over.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: Nautical instrument still initially in existence

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word still

parts.note: extant means still surviving, in existence

explanation.surface: An old navigational device is, at first, still around.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator's device for measuring the angle of the sun or stars above the horizon.

clue.text: Break agreement, mix oil before stirring tea after five

indicators.note: after puts the rest following the five
before puts the oil piece ahead of the tea piece

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: mix tells us to scramble the letters of oil
stirring tells us to scramble the letters of tea

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: mix oil, then stir the tea after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' makes IOL from OIL and 'stirring' makes ATE from TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a treaty or rule is to breach it.

clue.text: Northerner wearing no make-up

indicators.note: make-up as the way something is made up, a reconstruction of the letters

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian goes without cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but is the anagram signal for WEARING NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Norway, in the far north of Europe.

clue.text: German lady in the idiot's clutches

indicators.note: the answer is held within the letters of 'the idiot's', as if grasped

explanation.surface: A woman from Germany is held tight by a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name in German-speaking countries, as in the children's story heroine.

clue.text: On one's guard about egg flung in mischievous jesting

indicators.note: about wraps the guarded word around the egg piece

parts.note: wary means cautious, on one's guard

indicators.note: flung shows the letters of egg are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Being careful while an egg is hurled during pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flung' makes GGE from EGG, placed inside WARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Waggish behaviour is joking or playful teasing.

clue.text: Singularly old medical care?

parts.note: the plural noun for treating the elderly, made singular, becomes an adjective meaning aged

explanation.surface: Unusually old-fashioned health treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatrics is medicine for the elderly; one elderly person, or anything very old, takes the singular form.

clue.text: Insignificant quartet went into test

indicators.note: went into places the quartet inside the test

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is the Roman numeral four, a quartet

explanation.surface: A four-piece band played a trifling audition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial things are minor and unimportant.

clue.text: I am to have a drink before Gareth loses his head, it is unreal

indicators.note: before puts the drink ahead of the man's name

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
gin is a drink

indicators.note: loses his head removes the opening letter

parts.note: Gary is a familiar form of the name Gareth

explanation.surface: I'll have a gin before Gareth is beheaded: a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth gives GARY, its pet form; 'loses his head' drops the G to leave ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unreal exists only in the mind.

clue.text: Number said to understand and know beforehand

indicators.note: said means spoken, giving the sound of the number

parts.note: four is a number
to see is to understand, as in 'I see'

explanation.surface: A count is spoken, then grasped, so one predicts.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to predict or anticipate.

clue.text: Qualification good sportspeople should have

definitions.meaning: suitability for a role, being fit for it

explanation.surface: Top athletes need a certain credential.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both suitability for a role and physical condition.

clue.text: Nonsense, it's cleaning liquid for our pupils

definitions.text: it's cleaning liquid for our pupils
definitions.meaning: pupils are in the eyes, so a rinse for them

explanation.surface: Teachers dismiss a school cleaning product as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is called this, and so is lotion for rinsing the eyes.

clue.text: Beggar disturbed opening door spoke boastfully

indicators.note: disturbed shows the letters of beggar are jumbled
opening picks the first letter of door

explanation.surface: A troubled vagrant at the front door shows off.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, so bragged is spoke boastfully.

clue.text: Whiskey biscuit

definitions.meaning: an American whiskey made mainly from corn
a British chocolate sandwich biscuit with chocolate cream filling

explanation.surface: A drink and something to dunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky's corn whiskey shares its name with a chocolate cream cookie sold in Britain.

clue.text: George Dunn went round cell

indicators.note: went round puts Dunn around the other piece

parts.note: the surname is taken as written

explanation.surface: One man circled another in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a prison cell, usually underground.

clue.text: Follow the trail

definitions.meaning: to follow, as in ... a suspect

explanation.surface: Pursue the path.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pursue; as a noun, a path or footprints.

clue.text: Kenneth holds a recipe for the lady

indicators.note: holds puts the short form around the other letters

parts.note: Ken is short for Kenneth
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'recipe', 'take'

explanation.surface: A man keeps a cooking formula for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name.

clue.text: Learning routine, I'd come unstuck

indicators.note: come unstuck means fall apart, so the letters break up and rearrange

explanation.surface: A rote approach to study falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning or scholarship.

clue.text: One gets endless darkness at home in the far north

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter

parts.note: gloom is darkness

explanation.surface: A person lives through perpetual night up in the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome dwelling built of snow blocks.

clue.text: Ancient state of Italy in the Potteries

definitions.meaning: the land of the Etruscans in central Italy
a district of Stoke-on-Trent, where Wedgwood built his works

explanation.surface: An old Italian region turns up in English pottery country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries are the pottery-making towns of Stoke-on-Trent in Staffordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscan homeland gave its name to Josiah Wedgwood's factory village in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Dotty type

parts.note: seems to mean a crazy person, but means printing made of raised dots

explanation.surface: A slightly mad person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactile writing system of raised dots read by blind people.

clue.text: Period of harmony after rematch?

parts.note: rematch reads as a sporting replay, but means a couple marrying again, then holidaying

explanation.surface: Peace following a replayed contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday a couple takes later in marriage to rekindle romance; here a remarried pair.
